text: Where does your food actually go after you swallow?
Acid and churning turn your meal into a thick liquid called chyme.
The liver and gallbladder add bile. The pancreas adds enzymes.
Then the small intestine. About twenty feet of it.
This is where most nutrients get absorbed.
Stomach plus small intestine: about six to eight hours.
Last stop, the large intestine. About five feet.
It pulls water out. That part alone takes about thirty-six hours.
Start to finish? Roughly two to five days.
